blocks.text: 1. ResNet
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445475210-999801127.png

GoogLeNet, the previous topic, achieved efficiency through parallel filters within each layer. ResNet solved a genuinely different problem: training networks that are dramatically deeper still, explored throughout this topic.
It works by introducing skip connections, a genuinely simple idea with genuinely enormous consequences, covered in complete depth throughout the rest of this topic.
2. The Degradation Problem
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445475211-658218224.png

A genuinely surprising, real problem connects back to Vanishing Gradients, already covered in Activation Functions and Gradient Clipping. Simply stacking more and more layers eventually made networks genuinely perform worse, not better.

This genuinely counterintuitive finding, where more capacity should logically help but instead genuinely hurt performance, is exactly the problem this entire topic addresses throughout the sections that follow.
3. Not Just Overfitting

This connects back to Overfitting, already covered in its own topic. This degradation genuinely was not overfitting: even training accuracy itself got worse with more depth, not just validation accuracy.

This is a genuinely surprising, distinct problem that demanded a genuinely different explanation, since overfitting, already covered, would normally show strong training performance alongside weak validation performance.

blocks.text: 4. The Skip Connection Idea
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445475211-722818247.png
ResNet's genuinely core idea adds the input of a block genuinely directly to its own output, skipping over the block's own layers entirely, a genuinely simple, direct structural change.
This is called a skip connection, or residual connection, the genuinely defining feature of this architecture, and the exact mechanism that gives ResNet its own distinctive name.
5. Why Skip Connections Genuinely Help

This connects back to Backpropagation, already covered in its own topic. Gradients can now genuinely flow directly backward through the skip connection itself, without necessarily passing through every single intermediate layer.

This directly bypasses the vanishing gradient problem, already covered, that genuinely plagued extremely deep networks, giving a genuinely direct, mathematical explanation for the degradation problem already covered earlier in this topic.

blocks.content: This direct gradient path, already covered in this topic, is genuinely the core mathematical reason ResNet successfully trained networks far deeper than any architecture already covered earlier in this module.

blocks.text: 6. Learning Residuals: An Elegant Reframing
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445475212-830228778.png

A genuinely elegant reframing connects back to weights, already covered throughout Backpropagation & Optimization. A block only needs to genuinely learn the difference from its own input, not the entire transformation from scratch.

This residual, the genuinely small adjustment on top of the input already covered in the previous section, is genuinely easier to learn than an entire transformation, explaining ResNet's own distinctive name.
7. The Ease Of Learning An Identity Mapping

blocks.alt: The Ease Of Learning An Identity Mapping
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445475212-293276566.png
This connects back to learning residuals, already covered in this topic. If a block genuinely needs to do nothing at all, it can genuinely learn to output exactly zero, a genuinely trivial target.

This makes the skip connection genuinely pass the input straight through unchanged, a genuinely trivial case to learn, directly explaining why extra, unnecessary depth no longer genuinely hurts performance the way it did before.
8. Extreme Depth, Genuinely Achieved
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445475213-743081109.png

A genuinely dramatic, real achievement connects back to VGG's own depth variants, already covered. ResNet enabled genuinely successfully training networks dramatically deeper than VGG or GoogLeNet ever achieved.

This genuinely dramatic increase in trainable depth, made possible entirely through the skip connection idea already covered throughout this topic, stands as one of ResNet's own most significant, lasting contributions.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing Why ResNet Is Genuinely So Influential

blocks.alt: Recognizing Why ResNet Is Genuinely So Influential
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445475213-126469473.png

This connects back to genuinely any task needing a genuinely deep, reliable feature extractor. Skip connections, already covered in this topic, became a genuinely standard component far beyond just image tasks.
This connects forward to Transformers, covered later in this course, and their own genuinely deep stacks. Skip connections, already covered, directly inspired similar techniques used there too.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates a genuinely simple skip connection in code, contrasting a block with and without one, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
block_input = rng.normal(size=5)
weights_1 = rng.normal(size=(5, 5)) * 0.01  # deliberately small, simulating an under-trained block
weights_2 = rng.normal(size=(5, 5)) * 0.01

def relu(x):
    return np.maximum(0, x)

def block_without_skip(x, w1, w2):
    h = relu(x @ w1)
    return relu(h @ w2)  # already covered as the degradation problem's own risk: information can genuinely get lost

def block_with_skip(x, w1, w2):
    h = relu(x @ w1)
    residual = relu(h @ w2)
    return x + residual  # already covered as the skip connection idea in this topic

output_without_skip = block_without_skip(block_input, weights_1, weights_2)
output_with_skip = block_with_skip(block_input, weights_1, weights_2)

print("Input:", np.round(block_input, 3))
print("Output without skip connection:", np.round(output_without_skip, 3))
print("Output with skip connection:", np.round(output_with_skip, 3))
print("\nWith an under-trained block, already covered in this topic, the skip connection keeps the output genuinely closer to the original input")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: ResNet solved the degradation problem: stacking more layers eventually made networks perform worse.
This degradation was not overfitting; even training accuracy itself got worse with more depth.
Skip connections add a block's input directly to its own output, skipping over its layers.
This gives gradients a direct path backward, bypassing the vanishing gradient problem.
Each block only needs to learn a residual, the difference from its own input, not a full transformation.
Learning to output zero lets a block pass its input through unchanged when extra depth is not needed.
ResNet enabled successfully training networks dramatically deeper than VGG or GoogLeNet.
Skip connections became a standard component used far beyond image tasks, including in Transformers.
Next up: DenseNet, an architecture that took the skip connection idea even further.
